text: Ingests events from any monitoring tool; alert rules turn matching events into alerts routed to the right team
quote: Teams configure Alert Triggers (see next section) to describe which events should alert and whom, and when a Rule matches, the Event is turned into an Alert and routed to the relevant party

text: Accepts events from a standard webhook when the payload matches the expected event format
quote: you can also create events by using a standard webhook and ensuring the data matches the expected Event Format.

text: Integrates with alerting and monitoring tools to create incidents automatically from alerts
quote: Integrate with alerting and monitoring integrations to automatically create incidents from alerts

text: Backtests alert rules against past events using a CEL query in the filter builder
quote: On the Alert Rules page, you can quickly run a backtest of events by running a CEL query in the page's filter builder.

text: Escalation policies define how alert notifications reach team members, through on-call schedules or to individuals
quote: Escalation policies define how notifications from an Alert are sent to various team members, either as part of an on-call schedule or as an individual.

text: On-call schedules are built from rotations that define shift timing and assignment for a team
quote: Create schedules with rotation to manage your team's on-call

text: On-call schedule overrides are preserved
quote: Introducing: Preserved OnCall Schedule Overrides

text: Support hours can snooze alerts
quote: Support Hours Now Snoozes Alerts

text: Sends alert notifications by push, Slack, Microsoft Teams and email
quote: Notifications via push, Slack, Microsoft Teams, email

text: Can notify specific users and Slack channels directly
quote: FireHydrant also allows directly notifying specific users and Slack channels.

text: Webhook targets send alerts to external destinations
quote: **Webhook targets** on FireHydrant allow alerts to be sent to external destinations via a webhook.

text: Migrates existing PagerDuty or Opsgenie configuration into Signals
quote: New Signals Migrator: Migrate your PagerDuty or Opsgenie config in minutes

text: Alerting analytics show how events become alerts, how many are acknowledged, and how many become incidents
quote: Use our new Alerting Analytics page to understand how incoming events are turning into Alerts, how many alerts are being acknowledged, and how many alerts are then turning into incidents.

text: Incident analytics can be filtered and grouped by service, environment, team, severity, user and custom fields
quote: FireHydrant's analytics offer the ability to filter and group by various aspects... Service, Environment, Functionality, Team, Severity, User, [Custom Field]

text: Automates manual tasks such as creating incident Slack channels, Jira tickets and meeting bridges
quote: Automate manual tasks such as creating incident Slack channels, Jira tickets, meeting bridges, and more

text: Runbooks are a condition-based automation engine that is evaluated whenever an incident is declared
quote: Runbooks are FireHydrant's automation engine. They define and automate a workflow of steps and actions according to specified conditions.

text: A default runbook attaches to every incident, assigns the opener as Commander and adds a task list
quote: The default Runbook will always have two default steps: Assign a Role... Add Task List

text: A runbook step can send a webhook or HTTP request to internal systems, for example to roll back a deployment
quote: This article explains how to set up a Runbook step that sends a webhook to an endpoint of your choice.

text: A runbook can post to a Slack channel when a new AI summary becomes available
quote: We'll use our runbook to then add a step with conditions for posting into Slack when a new summary has become available.

text: Responders can browse triggered runbooks from an incident Slack channel using /fh
quote: From Slack, inside an incident channel, you can browse the list of triggered Runbooks for this by executing `/fh`.

text: Features are available to everyone in the Slack workspace without needing a FireHydrant account
quote: Universal Access: Available to everyone in your Slack workspace, they don't need a FireHydrant account.

text: AI-generated incident summaries are created as soon as an incident is declared
quote: Dive into incidents with AI-generated summaries that provide a clear, concise overview of the situation. Perfect for bringing new responders up to speed in no time.

text: An Audiences feature tailors incident summaries to different stakeholder groups
quote: With our new Audiences feature, summaries can now be tailored to meet the specific needs of different stakeholder groups.

text: An AI Scribe joins incident bridges to transcribe discussions, supporting Zoom and Google Calendar
quote: After enabling, the FireHydrant Scribe will be invited to your meetings to capture crucial discussions and decisions made during incident bridges

text: AI captures key insights from Zoom chat
quote: Never miss a beat, even if you join late. Our AI captures essential Zoom chat insights, ensuring you're always in the loop.

text: Copilot compares ongoing incidents to past ones and makes suggestions in the Command Center and Slack
quote: FireHydrant's Copilot proactively compares ongoing incidents to your existing and previous incidents and makes suggestions in the Command Center and Slack.

text: Admins control whether AI is enabled in the tenant and for which features
quote: You will additionally have control over whether AI is available in your tenant, and for which features.

text: On resolution, AI drafts a retrospective with an overview, timeline, impacts and preliminary lessons learned
quote: Upon incident resolution, AI-Drafted Retrospectives generate a comprehensive draft that includes a structured overview of the incident, timelines, impacts, and preliminary Lessons Learned.

text: Draft with AI generates answers to individual retrospective template questions from incident data
quote: When you click "Draft with AI" next to any question in your retrospective template, FireHydrant will: Analyze the incident's timeline, details, and context

text: Multiple retrospective templates standardize post-incident reviews across incident types and teams
quote: Create and manage multiple templates to standardize your post-incident review process across different types of incidents or teams.

text: Enterprise retrospectives support real-time collaboration with presence indicators and live cursors
quote: Enterprise customers have access to the collaboration features in FireHydrant's Retrospectives, which include seeing who's on the document looking at it at any moment as well as live cursor updates

text: Each incident gets an internal ephemeral status page that collects updates posted from Slack or the Command Center
quote: each incident on FireHydrant will have a dedicated ephemeral status page that summarizes high-level details and includes key links. All incident notes/updates posted via Slack (`/fh update`) or via Command Center are posted to the Internal

text: Internal status pages for org-public incidents can be viewed without auth or a license
quote: For public (to your organization) incidents, these internal status pages do not require auth or a FireHydrant license to view.

text: Offers external status pages, hosted by FireHydrant or Atlassian, with unlimited public status pages
quote: The FireHydrant platform offers both internal status pages, which are meant for the internal team only and require no setup, as well as external status pages (Atlassian and FireHydrant-hosted).

text: Service catalog tracks services, environments and dependencies and pulls in responders based on the impacted area
quote: Keep track of your apps, services, environments, and their relationships, and automatically pull in responders based on impacted product area

text: Public API uses token-based API key authentication
quote: FireHydrant allows you to access the API with an API key using token-based authentication.

text: Anything you can do in the UI can be done through the API, including integrations, incidents and webhooks
quote: You can use the FireHydrant API to configure integrations, define incidents, and set up webhooks--anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI.

text: API keys act like a user and get Owner permissions by default
quote: An API key can perform actions like any other user, and by default, it will have Owner permissions.

text: Bot tokens act for a machine rather than a user, so integrations keep working when people leave
quote: FireHydrant supports bot tokens to act on behalf of a computer instead of a user's account. This prevents integrations from breaking when people leave your organization

text: A read-only API endpoint allows longer timeouts for complex queries, with up to 30s of lag
quote: Note that the read-only endpoint has a much longer timeout for retrieving more complex data, but may lag behind the primary endpoint by as much as 30s.

text: Publishes an OpenAPI 3.0 spec of the FireHydrant API
quote: The official freshworks-oss/firehydrant-mcp repository publishes a FireHydrant OpenAPI document (.speakeasy/openapi.output.yaml): openapi "3.0.1", info.description "An MCP server for interacting with FireHydrant's API", servers https://api.

text: Provides an official MCP server for interacting with the FireHydrant API
quote: Official FireHydrant MCP server

text: Webhooks send internal events or custom commands to external systems
quote: FireHydrant enables you to create webhooks that respond to internal events or custom commands to send information to external systems.

text: The fhcli command-line tool records change events, such as Docker builds, Jenkins deploys and CI statuses, from CI systems
quote: FireHydrant provides a command line tool, `fhcli`, to easily submit changes from your existing CI or orchestration systems. You can use `fhcli` to record the creation of Docker images, deploy events in Jenkins, CI build statuses

text: Audit logs record runbook changes, incident declarations, logins and other events for security and audit
quote: Audit logs give organizations transparency and visibility into the events happening on the FireHydrant platform. From Runbook modifications to incident declarations, logins, and more

text: Supports SAML 2.0 single sign-on through an identity provider
quote: If you have an identity provider (IDP) that supports SAML 2.0, you can use it with FireHydrant as a single sign-on provider.
